A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Direct-LLaVA study and support a complete comparison. Sections, equations, Tables 1–11, Figures 1–7, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–D can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, visual-input removal experiments, qualitative examples, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same architecture, image/text reconstruction tasks, directed-token placement, and Image-to-Response Guided loss. Equations 1–14 and Algorithm 1 specify unchanged training procedures.

E1.justification: The main benchmark coverage and appendix experiments using LLaVA-OneVision data, AI2D, and MMBench already appear in v1. The added mention of human brain signals concerns prior work, not an evaluated domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Shikra, IDEFICS, Qwen-VL variants, and LLaVA variants in their respective tables. Appendix comparator sets also remain unchanged; added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–B retain the same model configurations, training-data budgets, shuffling settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures. These include middle-frame video evaluation and the 50% versus 100% pretext-data settings.

E4.justification: The backbone, token selection and placement, training-phase shuffling, guided-loss, data-size, and permutation-count analyses are all present in both versions. The visual-input removal experiment and qualitative case studies are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–11 and the figures' reported findings are unchanged. For example, Direct-LLaVA with Vicuna-13B retains 77.3 on SciQA-IMG, 65.4 on TextVQA, and 1572.1 on MME; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, permutation formulation, and objectives in Equations 1–14 remain equivalent. Changes to argmax typesetting do not alter the mathematics, and no proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about shuffle learning, directed tokens, guided loss, multimodal alignment, and state-of-the-art benchmark performance. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are retained. Appendix D still identifies unexplored loss balancing and limited model/data scale, while Appendix B still states that guided loss alone may not suffice for robust multimodal reasoning.

D1.justification: The front-page resource pointer changes from the laboratory homepage to the DirectedTokens project page. A new acknowledgment identifies the Arkansas High-Performance Computing Center as a GPU provider. Implementation settings and pseudocode remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: v2 adds ten references, including ViT, CYCLO, HIG, Bractive, and UMBRAE, and briefly mentions human brain signals. These expand background attribution without substantively revising the existing LLaVA and shuffle-learning positioning or novelty argument.

P1.justification: v2 adds an acknowledgment paragraph and an explicit Appendices heading, updates the publication footer to NeurIPS 2025, and makes small introductory edits. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes from a boxed grid to horizontal rules, and figure/table placement and surrounding text wrapping shift, including Figure 6 and Tables 5–6. All seven figures and eleven tables retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The added citations, acknowledgments, project-specific link, and layout adjustments provide small documentary conveniences. The scientific argument, all reported results, appendix analyses, and limitations remain unchanged, with no substantive clarification or evidential gap resolved. Overall paper quality is essentially unchanged.
